title: Luna on the Streets
voice_note: New narrator only; not a replacement for Luna's established character voice.

shots.text: Old Sacramento had a sound for everything. Riverboats. Bicycle bells. Boots on the boardwalk. And one very small dog, listening for a very big adventure.
This was Luna. Official shop greeter. Unofficial neighborhood detective. And, when nobody was looking, a highly trained inspector of suspicious snacks.
Today's case appeared to be a French fry. Golden. Abandoned. And clearly in need of immediate supervision.
Mike had a rule about street food. Luna had a question about why anyone would put perfectly good evidence on the street.
She checked the fry. She checked Mike. She checked the fry again. This investigation was going extremely well.
Then, underneath the boardwalk, something answered. Three tiny taps. A pause. Then three more.
Luna forgot to sniff. One ear tipped toward the wood. The other stayed on Mike, just in case he needed supervision too.
It wasn't a bicycle. It wasn't the river. And it certainly wasn't a French fry. French fries were usually much quieter.
She lowered her nose. Something cool brushed her whiskers. From the gap between two planks came a little flash of gold.
A brass key. Small enough to lose. Old enough to have a story. And right at the top, a tiny paw print.
Luna looked at her own paw. Then at the key. Well. That was either a coincidence, or someone had very good taste.
Under the boards, where the sunset couldn't quite reach, a small brass box waited in the dust.
Its lock held the faintest blue light. Not bright enough for a person to notice. Exactly bright enough for Luna.
Mike was still beside her. The shop was still warm behind them. But the ordinary afternoon had quietly become something else.
The tapping stopped. The key gave one last little shiver. And somewhere below, a latch clicked.
For once, Luna forgot all about the fry.
